# naturind

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/brummkyl/naturind/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/brummkyl/naturind/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![License: GPL v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GPL%20v3-blue.svg)](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0)
![Version 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.0.0-white)
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of naturind is to support the calculation of performance indicators
that may be used to evaluate the performance of existing protected areas and expansion priorities identified using spatial prioritization algorithms.

## Installation

You can install the development version of naturind like so:

``` r
install.packages("remotes")
library(remotes)
remotes::install_github("brummkyl/naturind", upgrade = "never)
library(naturind)
```

## Key functions

Performance indicators (and their associated metrics) can be calculated using the provided 'pi.--' functions. A limited number of helper functions ('create.--') are also available to support the creation of required input parameters, including transboundary buffers ('tb.buffers' parameter --> 'pi.transboundary') and planning unit-by-region lookup tables ('--.sub2' parameters --> 'pi.evp'; 'pi.mta'; 'pi.rpz').

## Outputs

After running any of the 'pi.--' functions, outputs will automatically be saved to the current .Rproject, or working directory. These .csv files are saved using user-defined 'project.name' and 'version' parameters as a built-in version control and naming convention. The files are stored to the "performance_outputs/version" subfolder.
